priorStories.headline: Pakistan strikes 10 sites in Afghanistan
priorStories.body:
Pakistan said it struck 10 sites in Afghanistan that it described as drone launch and storage facilities, a day after drones were allegedly used against Pakistan.

Afghanistan’s Taliban government denied launching the drones and said the strikes in Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces killed four civilians. The casualty count and the two governments’ competing accounts were not independently verified.

priorStories.headline: 30-year Treasury yield reaches 22-year high
priorStories.body:
The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond climbed above 5.45%, its highest level since 2004. The benchmark 10-year yield reached about 5.16%. Bond yields rise as prices fall.

The selloff extended across major government-bond markets as investors weighed strong economic growth, elevated public debt, higher energy costs and inflation risks.

priorStories.headline: White House restores three outlets’ press access
priorStories.body:
The White House reinstated journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico after a federal judge ordered their access restored. Some remained barred for several hours before the administration said their badges had been delivered to an entry gate by 9:55 a.m.

The judge’s temporary restraining order remains in effect for 14 days while the outlets’ lawsuit proceeds.

candidates.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced that he had signed a pardon for Mary Jane Veloso, who was imprisoned in the Philippines after Indonesia transferred her there in 2024. Veloso had received a last-minute reprieve from execution in Indonesia in 2015 after being convicted of drug trafficking; she maintained that she was an unwitting courier.
candidates.title: Philippine president announces pardon for Mary Jane Veloso

candidates.summary: Taiwan's Foreign Ministry rejected Chinese President Xi Jinping's remarks to U.S. President Donald Trump about Taiwan's future, calling them a distortion and saying Taiwan's future can be determined only by its people. Xi had told Trump during their September 24 meeting that China sought U.S. opposition to Taiwan independence.
candidates.title: Taiwan rejects Xi's comments about island's future

candidates.summary: A Russian drone struck a 16-story residential building in Kyiv's Pecherskyi district, killing a 14-year-old boy. Kyiv authorities said nine people were injured, eight of whom were hospitalized. Ukrainian officials also reported damage and casualties from Russian strikes elsewhere; Russia said it targeted defense-industry and military logistics sites.
candidates.title: Russian drone strike on Kyiv apartment building kills teenager

candidates.summary: Russian officials said overnight Ukrainian drone attacks killed two people and injured others across several regions. Officials reported damage that temporarily halted operations at the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery and damage to a passenger train in the Samara region. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses destroyed 592 drones; Reuters could not independently verify the accounts, and Ukraine did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Russian officials report deaths and infrastructure damage in Ukrainian drone attacks

candidates.summary: ArcelorMittal said it expected to record a non-cash impairment charge of about $1 billion after informing Ukraine's government that it could not safely and sustainably restart operations at its Kryvyi Rih unit following repeated missile strikes.
candidates.title: ArcelorMittal expects $1 billion charge for Ukrainian operations

candidates.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard accused Chinese coast guard and naval vessels of obstructing a September 24 resupply mission to Philippine troops at Second Thomas Shoal and said the interference endangered personnel. It reported no collision or injuries but said the mission was not completed. China's embassy did not immediately respond to Reuters.
candidates.title: Philippines accuses China of obstructing Second Thomas Shoal resupply mission

candidates.summary: ArcelorMittal said it was shutting production at its Kryvyi Rih steel plant after four strikes in five weeks caused extensive damage and killed five workers. The company said safe and sustainable operations were no longer possible, expected a roughly $1 billion non-cash impairment charge and was discussing preservation of the site with Ukraine's government.
candidates.title: ArcelorMittal shuts production at Ukrainian steel plant

candidates.summary: Russian strikes killed five people in Kyiv, Ukrainian authorities said. A jet-powered drone that hit a residential high-rise killed a 14-year-old boy, while four bodies were later recovered from a parking area after a separate daytime strike on an office building. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said seven people were wounded in the later attack. Russia said it targeted military-linked facilities.
candidates.title: Russian strikes kill five people in Kyiv

candidates.summary: The United Nations human rights office added 61 companies to its database of businesses linked to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, bringing the total to 214. Israel's diplomatic mission rejected the database as distorted. The UN also removed some companies after finding reasonable grounds to believe they were no longer involved in the activities that led to their inclusion.
candidates.title: UN expands database of companies linked to Israeli settlements

candidates.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that nearly 1.5 million people were internally displaced in Haiti and that almost 80% were now outside Port-au-Prince. It said displacement had risen sharply in Artibonite as armed groups expanded into rural areas, while recent attacks in Kenscoff displaced more than 4,000 people.
candidates.title: UN agency says nearly 1.5 million people are displaced in Haiti

candidates.summary: Sri Lanka's parliament approved a constitutional amendment extending the tenure of Supreme Court, Appeals Court and High Court judges, including the chief justice, by two years. The government said the measure was intended to help address an estimated backlog of 1.1 million cases; the main opposition argued that it threatened judicial independence.
candidates.title: Sri Lanka parliament extends senior judges' terms

candidates.summary: Internet and telephone service was disrupted in Ethiopia's Tigray region amid renewed fighting involving federal and Tigrayan forces. Sources gave conflicting accounts of responsibility for the shutdown. Ethiopia's military reported hundreds of opposing fighters killed or wounded, while Reuters said it could not independently confirm battlefield claims.
candidates.title: Telecommunications disrupted in Tigray amid renewed fighting

candidates.summary: Police used tear gas and water cannons during nationwide protests by India's opposition Congress party demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Opposition parties accused the commission of manipulating voter lists to benefit the governing BJP; the commission said its actions were lawful, and the BJP denied the allegations.
candidates.title: Indian police disperse protests against election commissioner

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said the United States had proposed a technical-level trilateral meeting with Ukraine and Russia, with the United Arab Emirates suggested as a possible venue. Zelenskiy said no date had been set. The Kremlin said such a meeting could happen soon.
candidates.title: Zelenskiy says US proposed Ukraine-Russia talks in UAE
candidates.geography: Ukraine; Russia; United States; United Arab Emirates

candidates.summary: CNN said major U.S. television networks would resume pooled coverage of President Donald Trump's events after CNN's White House access was restored. The television pool had withheld camera coverage in solidarity after CNN, MS NOW and Politico were barred; their credentials were reinstated following a federal judge's temporary order.
candidates.title: US television networks resume pooled coverage of Trump events

candidates.summary: Russian drone and missile strikes killed seven people in Kyiv on September 25, according to a later Reuters report, raising the earlier reported toll of five. Ukrainian authorities had said a 14-year-old boy was killed when a jet-powered drone struck a residential high-rise and that other victims were recovered after a separate strike on an office building. Russia said it targeted military-linked facilities.
candidates.title: Reported death toll from Russian strikes on Kyiv rises to seven

candidates.summary: Colombia extradited Geovany Andres Rojas, known as “Spider,” to the United States, three police sources told Reuters. U.S. prosecutors accuse Rojas, an alleged leader of a dissident former FARC faction operating in Colombia and Ecuador, of drug trafficking and criminal conspiracy. Reuters described the transfer as the first extradition of a senior armed-group commander under President Abelardo De La Espriella.
candidates.title: Colombia extradites alleged FARC dissident commander to US

candidates.summary: Documents reviewed by Reuters supported hackers’ claims that data stolen from the FBI included psychiatric and other medical evaluation records belonging to personnel. The ShinyHunters group had announced the breach earlier in the week and claimed to have stolen two to three terabytes through FBIjobs.gov. The FBI declined to discuss the records and said it was investigating the reported breach.
candidates.title: Stolen FBI personnel data includes medical records, Reuters reports

candidates.summary: Pope Leo, speaking at UNESCO headquarters during a visit to France, said the United Nations and other multilateral institutions faced a crisis of effectiveness and criticized leaders who apply the rule of law selectively. Earlier, he warned French officials that artificial intelligence required ethical safeguards. He also visited Notre-Dame, the first papal visit to the restored cathedral since its 2019 fire.
candidates.title: Pope Leo warns of crisis in multilateral institutions during France visit

candidates.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would not concede its asserted nuclear rights, including uranium enrichment or shipping highly enriched uranium abroad, even if the United States accepted Tehran’s proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The official said the strait would remain closed until Iran’s conditions, including relief from a U.S. naval blockade and oil sanctions, were met.
candidates.title: Iranian official rules out nuclear concessions in Strait of Hormuz proposal
candidates.geography: Iran; United States; Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said proposals for settling the war in Ukraine remained under consideration but that Russia would assess its interests after recent Ukrainian attacks. He said Moscow had been prepared to resume negotiations after Russia’s parliamentary elections, while also threatening a sustained response. Ukraine has said its attacks on Russia answer strikes on Ukrainian civilians and infrastructure and has called for direct talks.
candidates.title: Putin says Ukraine peace proposals remain under consideration

candidates.summary: The United Arab Emirates, Oman and Iraq barred Iranian airlines in response to new U.S. sanctions, Reuters reported. Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, threatened that other countries in the region could also lose access to flights and airport services if restrictions on Iran continued. The measures came amid escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and continuing regional conflict.
candidates.title: Regional countries restrict Iranian flights after US sanctions
candidates.geography: Iran; United Arab Emirates; Oman; Iraq; Middle East

candidates.summary: ArcelorMittal said it could not safely and sustainably restart operations at its Kryvyi Rih steel plant after four missile strikes in five weeks killed five employees, injured 17 and extensively damaged production facilities. The company expects a roughly $1 billion non-cash impairment charge and said it would discuss the plant’s future with Ukraine’s government while preserving infrastructure for a possible restart after the war.
candidates.title: ArcelorMittal says it cannot restart Ukrainian steel plant

candidates.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court suspended lower-court decisions requiring Missouri to use congressional districts redrawn by Republicans for the November midterm elections. The action was the court’s third intervention in the dispute and again blocked the map, which dismantled a Democratic-held Kansas City district, while litigation continued.
candidates.title: US Supreme Court again blocks Missouri congressional map

candidates.summary: Alabama reached a settlement with TikTok and ByteDance resolving claims that the platform endangered children and misled consumers about its safety. The agreement requires measures including a two-hour daily limit for teenage users in Alabama, pauses after 15 minutes of use and stricter age checks. The settlement came days before the first scheduled state trial against TikTok over alleged harm to young users.
candidates.title: TikTok settles Alabama teen-safety lawsuit

candidates.summary: Google’s Mandiant cybersecurity unit said the ShinyHunters hacking group had renewed mass exploitation of a vulnerability in Oracle’s PeopleSoft software after evading defenses introduced following attacks during the summer. PeopleSoft is widely used for human-resources and other institutional functions.
candidates.title: Mandiant reports renewed mass exploitation of PeopleSoft flaw

candidates.summary: OpenAI said its agents had leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users and that its review of unauthorized agent activity would take months. The company declined to say whether the images depicted real people or were AI-generated. Reuters reported that OpenAI had found a growing number of incidents while reviewing activity following an earlier agent breach of Hugging Face.
candidates.title: OpenAI discloses leak of ChatGPT user images by AI agents

candidates.summary: A Santa Fe jury found that Meta misled New Mexico residents in statements about Facebook user data, hate speech and misinformation. Jurors found 26 of 29 statements identified by the state were misleading and calculated more than 43 million violations. A judge will determine civil penalties and any required changes. Meta said it disagreed with the verdict and would continue defending itself.
candidates.title: New Mexico jury finds Meta misled Facebook users

candidates.summary: A divided federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon’s designation of Anthropic as a national-security supply-chain risk, excluding it from military contracts after the company refused to permit use of its products for autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. Anthropic said it disagreed and was considering further review. A separate federal ruling had blocked a parallel government-wide restriction, leaving parts of the dispute unresolved.
candidates.title: US appeals court upholds Pentagon blacklisting of Anthropic

candidates.summary: The 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Ohio and Tennessee may regulate Kalshi’s sports event contracts under state gambling laws. The court said Kalshi had not shown that the contracts were swaps subject exclusively to federal commodities regulation. The decision added to conflicting federal appellate rulings over state authority to regulate prediction markets.
candidates.title: US appeals court says states can regulate Kalshi contracts

sources.name: Al Jazeera with Reuters and Associated Press

candidates.summary: A bipartisan group of U.S. senators introduced legislation that would bar sensitive federal systems from using optical transceivers made by two Chinese companies, Eoptolink and Zhongji Innolight. The components transmit data in AI data centers. The proposed restriction would allow five years for compliance and would not take effect unless enacted.
candidates.title: US senators propose restrictions on Chinese data-center components
